definition: Neural operators are a class of deep learning architectures designed to learn maps between infinite-dimensional function spaces.
details: Neural operators represent an extension of traditional artificial neural networks, marking a departure from the typical focus on learning mappings between finite-dimensional Euclidean spaces or finite sets. Neural operators directly learn operators between function spaces; they can receive input functions, and the output function can be evaluated at any discretization. The primary application of neural operators is in learning surrogate maps for the solution operators of partial differential equations (PDEs), which are critical tools in modeling the natural environment. Standard PDE solvers can be time-consuming and computationally intensive, especially for complex systems. Neural operators have demonstrated improved performance in solving PDEs compared to existing machine learning methodologies while being significantly faster than numerical solvers. Neural operators have also been applied to various scientific and engineering disciplines such as turbulent flow modeling, computational mechanics, graph-structured data, and the geosciences. In particular, they have been applied to learning stress-strain fields in materials, classifying complex data like spatial transcriptomics, predicting multiphase flow in porous media, and carbon dioxide migration simulations. Finally, the operator learning paradigm allows learning maps between function spaces, and is different from parallel ideas of learning maps from finite-dimensional spaces to function spaces, and subsumes these settings as special cases when limited to a fixed input resolution.

explainer.lead: Neural operators learn maps between infinite-dimensional function spaces, rather than between fixed-size vectors. They matter because one trained operator can output a solution that can be evaluated at any discretisation.

tiers.eli5: Instead of learning answers for one fixed grid, it learns the whole rule that turns an input curve into an output curve, so you can query it anywhere.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers train them as surrogate maps for the solution operators of partial differential equations, then evaluate the output at whatever resolution is needed. A pitfall is assuming accuracy transfers to discretisations unlike those seen in training.
tiers.paperLevel: Neural operators are deep learning architectures that directly learn operators between function spaces, taking input functions and producing output functions evaluable at any discretisation; they depart from learning maps between finite-dimensional Euclidean spaces or finite sets.

explainer.example: A neural operator is trained on solutions of a PDE and then, for a new input function, produces an output function that can be sampled on a finer grid than training used.
